main_body: Iron anvil: a flat-topped working face with a horn on the left, a dark narrow waist and a base with a light bar. A hot piece of iron sits on top.
top_band: light grey-white band at rows 5-6 (about 2 rows) across the working face; there is no deeper horizontal surface behind or below it
evidence: Down the middle column I see the red and orange glow at rows 2-4, a light grey band at rows 5-6, a mid grey face at rows 7-8, a dark waist at rows 9-11 and a base at rows 12-13. The top is only 1-2 rows, so it reads as a thin cap line rather than a foreshortened surface. There is no distinct front-edge line and no shadow under the edge. The waist and base are flat vertical shapes drawn straight from the front, like a profile elevation. This fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The anvil is small and simple. The iron has only about 3-4 grey steps, and the waist and base are flat near-black fills with no grain or speckle. The outline and dark areas are neutral and near-black rather than a tinted dark material tone. Each tile carries few colours, well below the stall and well references, which have tile scallops, wood grain and many tones. It would look thinner and more sticker-like beside the references.
